subject: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist — Finovia trial decision criteria

Subject: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist — Finovia trial decision criteria

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — good conversation. Per our run-through, I wanted to capture the small set of performance / SLO items you asked us to confirm so you can take these into your internal review. I've attached a short checklist and the demo recording.

Quick recap of what we observed during the demo (baseline):
- Model: open-llama-70b-quant (demo variant)
- Observed p95 request latency (single-stream): ~120 ms with our micro-batching defaults
- Sustained throughput during demo: ~350 req/s on the dedicated pod used for the demo
- Concurrency: reached ~180 concurrent active sessions before queueing increased
- Streaming tail latency: incremental chunk latency ~20 ms

Finovia-proposed SLOs (as noted on the call):
- p95 latency <= 150 ms end-to-end for single-request generation (no heavy context)
- Sustained throughput target: 400 req/s during business hours (30% burst headroom)
- Support for 250 concurrent sessions with graceful queueing
- Streaming support for partial tokens with tail latency < 50 ms

Open items / risks we flagged:
1) Burst traffic patterns — need short (1–5 min) stress tests to validate autoscale + burst capacity behavior.
2) Prefix / KV cache warmup — cold starts can add ~200–400 ms per first request depending on model size.
3) Security / procurement steps — you mentioned SOC2 artifacts and a short compliance checklist (we can loop security).

Proposed next-step MAP to validate SLOs and get to a trial decision:
- Redwood to run a 48-hour benchmark (controlled) using your representative prompt set + traffic pattern (we will simulate your daytime burst profile). Deliverables: raw logs, p50/p95/p99 latencies, token cost estimate, and suggestions to meet your 400 req/s target.
- Finovia to share a canonical prompt subset (+ traffic shape CSV) and preferred test window next week.
- Joint kickoff call for the performance run (30–45m) — propose Tue 2026-03-16 10:00am PT or Wed 2026-03-17 2:00pm PT.

Attachments: redwood-post-demo-slo-checklist.pdf, demo-recording-20260310.mp4

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the kickoff and get Rishi to draft the benchmark plan.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0133

---
Note: If you want a different model quantization profile (more aggressive), we can include that in the benchmark matrix and show cost/latency tradeoffs.

Marissa — thanks for the write-up and recording. A few clarifying points from our infra side: 

1) Bursty traffic: our peak pattern is short spikes that hit ~6–8x baseline for 60–90 seconds (ad-hoc analytics + nightly batch). We need to understand how Redwood handles those short bursts without violating p95.
2) Streaming behavior is important for our UI — we need partial token delivery within ~50 ms, otherwise the UX is degraded.
3) Can you confirm whether the demo environment used dedicated GPUs or shared nodes? Is the 350 req/s for a single pod or cluster?

Procurement note: Priya will need a SOC2 + data retention statement before we engage legal. Also, if the benchmark shows sustained cost > our target, we may need to scope to a smaller model variant.

Also tagging a small internal ask: can you include a plan for Canary rollout (we prefer blue/green or traffic-split style) during the trial?

Thanks — Alex

Alex / Priya — hi, Rishi from SE here. I pulled together a compact benchmark plan and answers to your infra questions below. Attached: benchmark-plan.yaml (stub).

Answers to questions:
- Demo environment: the demo ran on a single dedicated pod (8xA100 equivalent) configured for moderate batching. The 350 req/s number is what that pod sustained during the interactive demo workload. For cluster-level capacity we can scale horizontally; a 2-pod cluster gave us ~650 req/s in our internal tests with similar model and config.
- Burst handling: Redwood supports short burst capacity via a combination of autoscale burst pools and graceful queueing. In the benchmark plan we’ll run 60–120s spike tests at 6x and 8x baseline to show p95 impact and time-to-recover. We’ll report the percent of requests that experience queueing vs delayed response.
- KV cache / cold-starts: plan includes a warmup phase that pins common prefixes to evaluate steady-state p95. We’ll measure cold-start impact separately and quantify the tail.
- Streaming: we stream token diffs with kernel-level optimizations — incremental chunk latency in our tests is ~15–25 ms depending on sequence length. We’ll include a streaming-focused subtest to validate <50 ms tail latency under load.

Proposed benchmark matrix (high level):
- Test 1: Steady-state 400 req/s for 2 hours (measure p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU util, token cost)
- Test 2: Burst tests: 1 minute and 3 minute spikes at 6x and 8x baseline
- Test 3: Concurrency ramp to 250 active sessions, measure queue depth and time-to-serve
- Test 4: Streaming tail-latency test with typical chat prompts

MAP items we will deliver after the run:
- Raw logs and aggregated latency histograms
- Autoscaling recommendations (pod size, burst pool thresholds)
- Cost estimate per 1M tokens and suggested quantization options that meet p95 target
- Canary rollout checklist for your infra team (traffic-split settings, circuit-breaker thresholds, fallback model variants)

Next steps I propose:
1) Finovia shares prompt subset + traffic CSV and confirms preferred test window.
2) Kickoff call to align the run and security checkpoint — I can run the kickoff and then schedule the benchmark run.

If this looks good I’ll start filling the YAML with exact load generator config.

- Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
